title: SLO-bump Roadmap Triage Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook captures a compact operational process for when roadmap timing needs an SLO bump (temporary relaxed SLO) to unblock launches without compromising long-term reliability. It is intended for product-ops, release engineers, and release owners who must triage tradeoffs between time-to-market and platform stability.

Scope and audience:
- Applies to feature releases where performance/cost/latency SLO conflicts arise within 8 weeks of planned ship.
- Primary owners: product-ops (coordination), release engineer (platform impact), product manager (prioritization).
- Stakeholders: eng-serving-runtime, site-reliability-engineering, customer-success for high touch customers.

Executive summary (one-paragraph):
When a planned release cannot meet existing SLOs due to capacity, model variance, or infra constraints, use the SLO-bump flow below. The goal is to create a timeboxed, observable, reversible SLO relaxation with explicit guardrails: (1) minimize user impact, (2) document acceptance criteria, (3) define rollback triggers, (4) ensure a follow-up remediation sprint is scheduled. This document defines the triage checklist, KPI acceptance bands, and an operational cadence for approvals and postmortem.

Key definitions (short):
- SLO-bump: a temporary, documented adjustment to one or more service-level objectives (latency/availability/error-rate) to permit a release.
- Threshold window: the window (e.g., 7 days) during which elevated risk is monitored.
- Remediation sprint: a committed follow-up engineering sprint to close the root cause and return SLOs to baseline.

KPI matrix (primary metrics to evaluate before/after bump):
- 95th percentile latency (ms) — baseline target: < 250ms; bump max: 400ms
- Error rate (5xx tokenized/gRPC) — baseline target: <0.15%; bump max: 0.5%
- Tail token cost ($/1000 tokens) — baseline target: <$0.08; bump max: <$0.12
- Request queue depth (per-node) — baseline target: < 20; bump max: < 40
- Customer-impact score (qualitative 0–5) — baseline target: 0–1; bump max: 2

Decision heuristics (quick):
- Allow SLO-bump if: release unlocks >$50K ARR in first 90 days OR prevents >30% feature regressions for enterprise customers AND the bump does not exceed defined bump max for two or more primary KPIs simultaneously.
- Deny bump if: expected customer-impact score >=3 or no scheduled remediation sprint within two sprints.

Triage playflow (step-by-step):
1) Initial assessment (owner: release owner) — capture failing KPI(s), root cause hypothesis, and proposed bump dimensions. Document in ticket PRD-1173.
2) Platform impact review (owner: release engineer + eng-serving-runtime) — run a quick capacity forecast using the 7-day traffic simulator. Estimate cost delta.
3) Customer risk assessment (owner: customer-success) — check active customers affected and contractual SLAs. Attach mitigation notes.
4) Rapid ops review meeting (15 minutes) — attendees: product-ops, release owner, SRE lead, platform eng. Goal: approve/deny provisional bump within 24 hours.
5) If approved: enact temporary SLO change in monitoring (tagged bump_id) and create a realtime dashboard slice for the release (include 95/99 latencies, error rate, queue depth).
6) Monitoring & gating (owner: SRE) — monitor bump window, apply automated rollback if any hard rollback trigger fires (see triggers).
7) Post-bump retrospective and remediation commitment (owner: product manager) — within seven days after the bump window ends, publish RCA and confirm remediation sprint assignment.

Operational checklist (copyable, mark completed):
- [ ] Release owner documented KPI delta and justification in ticket
- [ ] Platform impact reviewed with forecast and cost delta
- [ ] Customer-success filed impact notes and temporary customer communication plan
- [ ] 15-min rapid ops meeting held and decision recorded (approve/deny)
- [ ] Monitoring slice created and bump_id tagged on metrics
- [ ] Automated rollback rules configured in observability (thresholds and cooldown)
- [ ] Release note updated with bump rationale and expiry date
- [ ] Remediation sprint scheduled (sprint id attached)
- [ ] Post-bump RCA published within 7 days

Automated rollback triggers (example thresholds):
- Any 5-minute window with error-rate > 1.0% for the release-tagged routes
- 99th percentile latency > 2x baseline for > 30 minutes
- Sustained queue depth > bump_max for > 10 minutes despite autoscaling
When trigger fires: SRE runs autopatch: route traffic to fallback model variant, scale up burst pool, and if no improvement within 12 minutes, initiate traffic cutover to canary/previous model and notify stakeholders.

Communication templates (short snippets to paste):
- Internal Slack (ops channel): "SLO-BUMP [bump_id] approved for release X. Bump window starts 2025-03-05T10:00Z. Watch dashboards: /dashboards/release-X-bump. Rollback triggers configured. PM: @Priya. SRE on-call: @Liam."
- Customer note (CS-run): "We are rolling out an update to <feature> with a short-term performance adjustment to ensure reliability across all customers. This will be temporary and we will restore baseline performance within two sprints. Contact CS for impact details."

Risk register (top 5 quick items):
1) High variance model behavior on long contexts — mitigation: route long-context traffic to a guarded variant.
2) Burst-induced autoscale delays — mitigation: warm reserved burst nodes pre-rollout.
3) Hidden cost spike — mitigation: advance cost alerting and daily cost cap during bump window.
4) Regressed evaluation metrics (quality drop) — mitigation: run reference prompt set before rollout and compare embedding/rerank scores.
5) Missed remediation — mitigation: remediation sprint gated to release milestone and tracked in product-ops board.

SLO-bump lifecycle example (timeline):
Day -7 to -1: triage, platform forecast, CS outreach
Day 0: approval, tag bump_id, enable dashboard and alerts
Day 0–7: monitoring window (active)
Day 8–10: retrospective, RCA, remediation sprint planning
Within 60 days: remediation completed, SLO restored, final postmortem published

Owner matrix (roles and responsibilities):
- Product-ops: coordinator and documentation keeper
- Release owner/PM: business decision, remediation owner
- Release engineer: rollout plan, observability tagging
- SRE: automated rollback, monitoring, runbook execution
- Eng-serving-runtime: technical mitigation work (variants, batching policy adjustments)
- Customer-success: customer comms, impact triage

How to use this doc (practical):
- Save as the canonical doc for any release seeking an SLO-bump. Create a bump_id like "BUMP-2025-03-04-XX" and append to ticket title.
- Keep the monitoring dashboard link in the ticket and in the Slack ops message.
- Update KPI values in the ticket rather than this master doc; this playbook defines process and guardrails.

Appendix A — Quick KPI snapshot template (paste into ticket):
KPI | Baseline | Proposed bump | Justification | Rollback trigger
95p latency | 230ms | 360ms | model variant memory growth at N=512 | 99p > 2x baseline for 30m
Error rate | 0.12% | 0.45% | batcher backpressure under peak traffic | error rate > 1.0% (5m)
Token cost | $0.072 /k | $0.11 /k | need to use single-precision variant to avoid OOM | daily cost cap $3k

Appendix B — Post-bump retrospective template (bullet answers):
- What changed technically?
- Which KPIs moved and by how much?
- Which rollback triggers fired (if any)?
- Customer impact notes and CS actions
- Root cause summary and remediation plan (owner + sprint)
- Lessons learned and checklist updates

Notes and history:
Created after a Q4 incident where multiple dedicated releases overlapped with a capacity reclaim and caused unplanned latency spikes. This condensed playbook reflects learnings to reduce approval latency while increasing observability and automated rollback discipline.

short_summary: Compact playbook for triaging temporary SLO relaxations tied to roadmap releases: decision heuristics, KPI bands, automated rollback triggers, and an operational checklist.
